subject: [PATCH v2] mm/memcontrol: skip non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats on the default hierarchy

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: Reviewer Yosry Ahmed questioned whether the added complexity of handling hierarchy changes is necessary for the optimization to work when switching from v2 to v1, suggesting an alternative approach using a boot parameter instead.
reviews.raw_body:
I wonder if the complexity is warranted for this optimization to work
when switching from v2 -> v1, or if we should just query the boot
parameter.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a race condition pointed out by Sashiko, agreed to drop the default hierarchy optimization for v3 and instead query the boot parameter.
reviews.raw_body:
I think you're right that we should just query the boot parameter.
Sashiko pointed out a race [1] in the opposite direction between the
flush and the bind where the flush can overwrite the local[i] value
stored by the bind, which is much worse than the above case where the
bind overwrites the local[i] value stored by the flush.

I'll drop the default hierarchy stuff for v3.

Thanks,
Joanne

[1] https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260902205406.624782-1-joannelkoong%40gmail.com

2026-09-02.patch_summary: This patch optimizes memory control group (memcg) statistics by skipping non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats on the default hierarchy, reducing flush costs and improving performance. The optimization is based on the observation that only legacy memory.stat and memory.numa_stat readers access these stats, which are not used on the default hierarchy. By skipping these stats, the patch reduces cacheline accesses and improves flush function performance by 2.2%. The change also includes a mechanism to handle cases where a controller is moved from the default hierarchy to the legacy v1 hierarchy at runtime.
